questions.q: What is the primary goal of technical writing?
questions.explanation: Technical writing is user-centered and aims to deliver clear, organized, actionable information.
options: To entertain the reader with creative storytelling.
To persuade the reader to change their political views.
To provide clear, organized, and actionable information.
To use complex vocabulary to demonstrate the writer's intelligence. word

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a typical example of a technical document?
questions.explanation: Poetry is expressive and creative, not technical.
options: A user manual for a smartphone.
A lyric poem about the Nile River.
A software API documentation.
A laboratory research report.

questions.q: In technical writing, "Audience Analysis" refers to:
questions.explanation: Audience analysis means understanding your readers’ background, needs, and level of expertise.
options: Counting how many people read your document.
Understanding the background, needs, and technical level of your readers.
Correcting the grammar and spelling of your coworkers.
Choosing the best font for a presentation.

questions.q: Which sentence follows the principles of technical writing best (conciseness and clarity)?
questions.explanation: Technical writing avoids wordiness; the simplest clear statement is preferred.
options: In view of the fact that the server is down, we should wait.
The server is currently experiencing a period of significant downtime.
Because the server is down, please wait.
At this point in time, the server is non-operational.

questions.q: Why do technical writers prefer using "Active Voice" (e.g., "The user clicks the button") over "Passive Voice" (e.g., "The button is clicked by the user")?
questions.explanation: Active voice is more direct and makes it clear who performs each action.
options: It makes the document longer and more professional.
It is more direct and clearly identifies who is performing the action.
It is the only way to write in English correctly.
Passive voice is never allowed in any situation.

questions.q: What is the purpose of using "White Space" in a document layout?
questions.explanation: White space increases readability and scannability by preventing visual clutter.
options: To save ink during the printing process.
To hide mistakes in the text.
To reduce visual clutter and make the document easier to scan and read.
It has no purpose; every inch of the page should contain text.

questions.q: If a software bug exists but is difficult to fix, a technical writer should:
questions.explanation: Accuracy and honesty require documenting known issues so users can anticipate them.
options: Ignore it and hope the user doesn't find it.
Document the issue clearly so the user knows what to expect.
Write that the bug is actually a "special feature."
Delete the section of the manual entirely.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes "Accessibility" in technical writing?
questions.explanation: Accessibility ensures the content can be used by people with varying abilities.
options: Making sure the file is not password protected.
Ensuring the document can be understood by people with different abilities (e.g., using Alt-text for images).
Writing the document in as many languages as possible.
Selling the manual at a very low price.
